clue.text: Roman eats cake, initially welcome after endless dance over

indicators.note: after says these letters follow the reversed dance in the answer
in an across clue 'over' says the dance word is turned round to read the other way
endless says the dance word loses its final letter

parts.note: the conga is a dance performed in a long line

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of cake is wanted

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome, a greeting

explanation.surface: A person in Rome is having cake and getting a welcome after a dance has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' and 'over' work on the dance, 'initially' takes from cake, and 'after' sets those letters behind it. 'Roman' looks like the subject of the sentence but goes with 'eats' as the definition: Roman-style food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi alla romana are semolina dumplings from Rome, so the dish is food in the Roman style.

clue.text: Maybe Jackson Pollock's essence embodied by e.g. swirling and splashing

indicators.note: embodied by means held in the body of, so one piece sits within the other
swirling stirs up the letters of e.g. into another order
the essence of a word is its core, here the central letter of Pollock
splashing throws the letters of and about into a new order

explanation.surface: Jackson Pollock's spirit lives on in his drip paintings, swirled and splashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' and 'splashing' each rearrange a short word, and 'embodied by' puts the central letter of Pollock inside the first. 'Jackson' is not the painter but the actor Glenda Jackson.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenda Jackson was an Oscar-winning actress and later a Labour MP, so her first name is an example.

clue.text: Work close to deadline in roofless museum

indicators.note: in places the last letter of deadline within the museum name
in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the museum name loses its first letter

parts.note: the Louvre is the great art museum in Paris

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the final letter of deadline

explanation.surface: Art is finished just before a deadline in a museum with no roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roofless' takes the L off LOUVRE, and 'close to' gives E, put inside OUVRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvre is the French-derived term for a body of work, or a single work, of an artist.

clue.text: Seeing snake in class, students perform a charm

indicators.note: in says the snake goes inside the word for class

parts.note: a caste is a social class, especially in Hindu society
the asp is a venomous snake, famous from Cleopatra
L is a learner, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: Pupils, spotting a snake in the classroom, recite a magic spell to protect themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' is a link meaning 'given that'. L for learner is doubled to make students plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a spell is to work magic, which is performing a charm or incantation.

clue.text: Nick and Denis both uncovered East Anglian rebels once

indicators.note: uncovered strips off the outer letters, and both says it happens to each of the two names

explanation.surface: Two men named Nick and Denis were exposed as historical rebels from Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both uncovered' strips the first and last letters from each name, leaving IC and ENI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were the Celtic tribe of Norfolk who, under Boudicca, revolted against Roman rule.

clue.text: Understood work books decline

parts.note: got can mean understood, as in 'I got the joke'
op is short for opus, a musical work
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A reader grasps that a literary work is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or falling into ruin.

clue.text: Iris's pair of gloves found on vale around Lake Superior

definitions.note: read as 'Iris is', the 's is a link and Iris is an example of the family the answer belongs to

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below, so the farewell comes after the glove letters
pair of takes the first two letters of gloves
around says the farewell word wraps the lake and superior letters

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye, which is adios in Spanish
U stands for upper class, superior

explanation.surface: Iris has two gloves, found in a valley near the great North American lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' is not a valley but Latin farewell, giving ADIOS; 'around' puts LU inside it. 'Lake Superior' looks like the Great Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus, or sword lily, belongs to the iris family, Iridaceae, so it is a relative of the iris.

clue.text: Damage ring

definitions.meaning: a ... is a cost or loss, as in 'the storm took its ...'

explanation.surface: A bell being damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll can be the harm suffered, and tolling is the sounding of a bell.

clue.text: Jack's target in this training beat that in Paris

parts.note: PE is physical education, training for the body
to tan is to beat or thrash, as in 'tan his hide'
que is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: A sailor sets his sights on a training exercise in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a sailor but is the small target ball in boules.
explanation.definitionFit: In petanque, the French form of boules, players throw metal balls as close as they can to a small ball called the jack.

clue.text: Wrong step during Twist?

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tress is a lock or plait of hair, a twist
pas is a step in ballet

explanation.surface: A misstep while doing the Twist, the 1960s dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like the dance but is a braid of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a sin or wrongdoing, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Play face-card of superior rank twice, thwarting game opponents

indicators.note: thwarting here has its old sense of lying across, so the pieces lie across between the two opponents

parts.note: in bridge, East and South sit next to each other on opposing sides
Q is the queen, a face card in a pack
U stands for upper class, of superior social rank
twice calls for the upper-class letter a second time, so it supplies another copy

explanation.surface: A card player keeps laying a high court card to frustrate the rival pair at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thwarting', in its old sense of lying across, puts QUU between E and S, two bridge players who sit as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is Peter Shaffer's stage drama about a boy who blinds horses.

clue.text: Part of Sgt Pepper uniform beginning to excite McCartney imitator?

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of excite is taken

parts.note: Paul McCartney of the Beatles
the suffix -ette marks an imitation, as in leatherette

explanation.surface: A Beatles tribute act wears a Sgt Pepper costume to thrill the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a mock Paul is a playful reading of the -ette suffix.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sgt Pepper costumes had shoulder ornaments of the military kind, each one an epaulette.

clue.text: Complaint maitre d' redressed, regularly wiping stains

indicators.note: redressed suggests putting the letters into new clothes, a new arrangement
regularly wiping says every other letter of stains is removed, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A head waiter, changing his clothes, grumbles while rubbing out marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redressed' turns MAITRED into DERMATI, and 'regularly wiping' strips S, A, N from stains to leave TIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatitis is skin inflammation, and complaint is a word for an ailment.

clue.text: Steal bank codes when withdrawing

indicators.note: withdrawing is drawing back, so the code word is read backwards

parts.note: PINs are personal identification numbers used for bank cards

explanation.surface: A thief nabs cash-card numbers while taking money out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns PINS round; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a bargain, and a steal is slang for something bought very cheaply.

clue.text: Spa place sprayed them with Chanel

indicators.note: sprayed suggests the letters are scattered like perfume into a new order

explanation.surface: At a health resort, guests were spritzed with Chanel perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham in Gloucestershire grew famous in the eighteenth century as a spa town with mineral springs.

clue.text: E-tailer's characteristic sitcom

definitions.meaning: an online shop never closes, so it is trading at any time of day or night
A BBC comedy set in a corner shop, starring Ronnie Barker

explanation.surface: An online retailer's defining feature is compared to a TV comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Round-the-clock trading is the mark of web shops, and the phrase is also the title of a British comedy series.

clue.text: Any swimming medley will entertain northern territory of old

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of Any moving about into a new order
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a salad is a medley, a mixture

explanation.surface: A swimming relay event will be put on for a region in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns ANY into NYA; 'medley' looks like the swimming race but is a mixture, SALAD, which takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was the British protectorate that became Malawi in 1964, so it is a former territory.

clue.text: Mocking beheaded French king, ascendant before

indicators.note: beheaded says the mocking word loses its first letter

parts.note: to banter is to tease or mock playfully

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascendant means rising, so the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: roi is French for king

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries jeer at a guillotined French monarch rising to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' cuts BANTER to ANTER and 'ascendant' turns ROI into IOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior means placed in front or earlier, the opposite of posterior.

clue.text: Advised one of five that mass-produces gifts for Easter?

definitions.meaning: British health advice is to eat five portions of fruit and vegetables a day, and this vegetable counts as one
a factory, or plant, making chocolate eggs could be called an ...

explanation.surface: A recommended item is part of a factory making Easter presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five' refers to the UK 'five a day' healthy-eating advice. The question mark marks the whimsical factory reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant, the US name for aubergine, is a vegetable recommended as part of a healthy diet.

clue.text: Old racer engine's all different, restricting learner Mike

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the other letters enclose these two
different says the letters are made into something else, a new order

parts.note: the letters of engine's, without the apostrophe
L is the learner plate on a car
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rebuilt car engine has been changed throughout, hampering a novice driver named Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ENGINESALL into NIGEANSELL, which 'restricting' wraps round LM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Mansell was a British Formula One champion of 1992, now retired from driving.

clue.text: Relative on remote islands third in event, given this?

definitions.text: Relative on remote islands third in event, given this?

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative
NZ, New Zealand, is a group of islands far from almost everywhere

indicators.note: third in says the third letter of event is taken

explanation.surface: A New Zealand relative who finished third in a competition receives this medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a relative coming third gets bronze.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze medal is awarded for finishing in third place in a competition.

clue.text: Patient's leg needs bandages, having turned red

indicators.note: having turned means the run of letters is read back to front
bandages means wraps up, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A patient's leg must be dressed, having become inflamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandages' finds SLEGNE inside the words, and 'having turned' reverses it. 'red' is not inflammation but a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto, and red is a common term for a communist.

clue.text: Show previous back surgery

parts.note: ex means former or previous, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: back says the word for surgery is turned round

parts.note: op is short for operation, a piece of surgery

explanation.surface: A demonstration of an earlier spinal operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the patient's spine but signals turning OP to PO.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition, a large public show of products or art.

clue.text: What flattens rabbit? Driver perhaps

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for talking on and on, which is to waffle
a driver is a golf club, and an iron is another kind of golf club

explanation.surface: A cartoonish question about squashing a bunny, with a motorist as the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is not the animal but rabbiting on, meaning chattering; 'Driver' is the golf club, not the motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A waffle iron is a hinged hot-plate that presses batter flat into a grid-patterned waffle.

clue.text: Plant life left to adorn marketplaces earlier

indicators.note: to adorn something is to decorate it, sitting within it

parts.note: fora is the Latin plural of forum, the marketplace of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Greenery was set out to decorate old market squares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' signals the ancient sense: Roman fora were public squares used as markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the plants of a region considered collectively, its plant life.

clue.text: Well-informed chef uses this most common ingredient in sweet

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan used by a chef
E appears twice in sweet, more than any other letter in it

explanation.surface: A clued-up cook knows what is used most in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredient' looks like food but means a letter: E is the one sweet holds most often.
explanation.definitionFit: Woke is slang for being alert to social issues, so aware and informed.

clue.text: Loved being alternative main speaker when short

indicators.note: alternative signals a different version of main, its letters arranged another way
when short says the speaker word loses its last letter

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Someone, being the substitute principal speaker, falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' turns MAIN into INAM, and 'when short' cuts ORATOR to ORATO.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover or beloved, a person who is loved.

clue.text: Money's quietly replaced by husband in the future

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter is swapped out for another letter

parts.note: pence are money, the 's standing for 'is'
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the P of PENCE for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence can mean from now on, as in 'a year hence', meaning a year later.

clue.text: Alsatian to be handled by militant plod again

indicators.note: being handled by something means being held in its grasp, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rad, short for radical, describes a militant
Alsace is French-speaking, and être is French for 'to be'

explanation.surface: A police dog is put in the care of a hard-line officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alsatian' is not the dog but a person from Alsace, in France; 'plod', the slang name for a police officer, is really a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To retread a path is to walk it once more, plodding over the same ground.

clue.text: Dove might be so innocuous around Hackney Marshes

indicators.note: Hackney is in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: something innocuous is harmless

explanation.surface: A dove, a peaceful bird, seems harmless in an East London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney Marshes are playing fields in East London; Cockneys say 'armless' for harmless. A dove, the symbol of peace, carries no arms, meaning weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove stands for peace, so it bears no weapons, a pun on arms as limbs and arms as weapons.
